I am a woman of fifty, farming this small piece of land my household owns here in the North West. Rice needs good care, so I will buy some urea and NPK from the market if the price is not too high — but I cannot afford too much, so I will stretch it across my plot. I save some manure from our animals and spread that too before planting. I use seed I bought last season from a neighbor who got the improved kind from the agro-dealer, because it gives better yield, and I will spray a little herbicide to save my back from weeding all alone. I have no irrigation here, we depend on the rains, and my daughters and I will do most of the work ourselves, but I will pay a few young men for transplanting and harvest days.
